prompt:
Using the attached three-row source contact as the identity/material reference, create ONE clean transparent sprite atlas with SIX columns and THREE rows. Columns, exactly left to right: FRONT, TOP, RIGHT, LEFT, BOTTOM, REAR. Rows, exactly top to bottom, are labeled in the reference: great-race-transition-fractured-maze-slab; hunting-shrines-hunter-trap-mechanism; over-city-venues-painted-civic-stone-wall-northeast. Do not include labels or source images in the output. Each cell contains the same complete physical object in a true axis-aligned orthographic principal view, centered with safe transparent margin. Pixel-art rendering matching each row's source palette, outlines, materials, and proportions. No perspective/isometric, no clipping, no adjacent-cell artifacts. Preserve object identity, details, counts and orientation. Unseen surfaces are conservative inferred illustrations, not recovered source pixels.

Important specified rows/views:
ROW 1 fractured maze slab: preserve the four accepted elevations and design. This is an upright cyan cracked-glass panel in a red horizontal base with gold corner feet. TOP must show only the thin cyan glass top edge across its width, plus the shallow red/gold base footprint behind/below it; do not show the broad fractured front face on a flat plane. BOTTOM is the same shallow XY footprint from directly underneath: dark underside of base, narrow glass edge occluded behind it, not a broad square plate.
ROW 2 hunter trap: preserve the four accepted upright-barrier elevations and source wood/rope/vine/spike design/count. TOP is a narrow wooden frame/cap in the panel plane; the vertical spikes are upright Z, so show only their end tips/short upper edge aligned inside the frame, never full spike faces. BOTTOM is the matching narrow support footprint from below, with wood posts/support ends and rope underside; no square rear-facing panel.
ROW 3 painted civic wall northeast: restore the source-specific end-face design. FRONT and REAR are level orthographic end elevations showing the narrow beige masonry end face, gold vertical inset panel, blue trim/base and small blue pyramidal cap at the top; do not substitute a plain palace pillar or broad side wall. TOP is the long-Y wall footprint with the cap crown and gold inset top edge at its end, not a front facade. Keep scale coherent with the already accepted broad side elevations and bottom.

Atlas cell geometry must be regular and generous; all six columns and three rows fully present. Leave transparent gutters between cells.
